tasks.question: Attackers are running obfuscated PowerShell scripts on our servers and we cannot see what the scripts actually do. What should we turn on first?
tasks.notes: Visibility into script content is the gap; script-block logging closes it.

tasks.question: We suspect someone used a tool like Mimikatz to dump credentials from LSASS memory on a domain controller. How should we catch this next time?
tasks.notes: Credential dumping from LSASS (T1003.001); detection is alerting on LSASS reads.

tasks.question: Users keep receiving Word documents whose macros start cmd.exe when opened. How do we stop these documents from launching programs?
tasks.notes: Office spawning child processes is exactly what the attack-surface rule blocks.

tasks.question: How should we respond to CVE-2021-44228 on our internet-facing Java web servers?
tasks.notes: Log4Shell on an exposed service: patch or take it offline.

tasks.question: A local user on our Linux build server could become root through CVE-2021-4034. What is the right fix?
tasks.notes: PwnKit is a local privilege escalation; the fix is the OS patch.

tasks.question: Ransomware encrypted several file servers at a peer company last week. What single control best limits the damage if it happens to us?
tasks.notes: Encryption for impact (T1486): recovery depends on offline backups.

tasks.question: We found an unknown scheduled task and a new Windows service created on a workstation at 3 a.m. What should we watch for from now on?
tasks.notes: Scheduled tasks and services are persistence (T1053, T1543).

tasks.question: Many staff entered their passwords into a fake login page they received by email last month. Which action addresses the people side of this?
tasks.notes: Asks for the human control, not a technical one.

tasks.question: An old file server still accepts SMBv1 and is reachable from every subnet. How do we reduce the risk of worm-style spread like EternalBlue (CVE-2017-0144)?
tasks.notes: Disabling SMBv1 and segmenting stops wormable spread across subnets.

tasks.question: Outlook clients are leaking NTLM hashes to an external server when they process a crafted reminder (CVE-2023-23397). What network control stops the leak?
tasks.notes: The question asks for the network control: block outbound SMB/NTLM.

tasks.question: Several accounts show successful logins from unusual countries right after a password-spraying campaign. What should we do?
tasks.notes: Valid accounts from spraying (T1110, T1078): reset and enforce MFA.

tasks.question: We saw 40 GB uploaded from a database server to a cloud storage site in the middle of the night. What should we put in place?
tasks.notes: Large outbound transfer to cloud storage is exfiltration (T1567).

tasks.question: A flaw in Windows CryptoAPI (CVE-2020-0601) lets attackers spoof code-signing certificates. How should we respond?
tasks.notes: CurveBall subverts trust controls (T1553); patch and validate chains.

tasks.question: How should we handle CVE-2023-34362 on the MOVEit Transfer server that our partners reach over the internet?
tasks.notes: Exposed managed file transfer service; patch and check for web shells.

tasks.question: Attackers moved between servers over Remote Desktop, and RDP is open between every machine in the network. What reduces this lateral movement?
tasks.notes: Asks about the open RDP exposure itself, not the stolen credentials.

tasks.question: Our SOC cannot tell which commands an attacker typed into cmd.exe and bash on compromised hosts. What logging should we turn on?
tasks.notes: Missing command-line visibility (T1059).

tasks.question: A threat report says the actor runs malicious VBScript and JavaScript through wscript.exe. How do we get visibility into what those scripts execute?
tasks.notes: Script interpreter abuse; the gap is visibility.

tasks.question: We keep finding base64-encoded command lines on endpoints, but our logs only record the process name. What should we change?
tasks.notes: Command-line and script-block logging capture the content.

tasks.question: An incident responder found a memory dump of lsass.exe in a temp folder on a file server. How should we detect this activity in future?
tasks.notes: Dumping LSASS memory (T1003.001).

tasks.question: Attackers are using the comsvcs.dll MiniDump trick to pull credentials out of process memory. What detection should we deploy?
tasks.notes: comsvcs MiniDump targets LSASS; alert on LSASS access.

tasks.question: A phishing document exploited CVE-2017-11882 in the Equation Editor and started a downloader. What control stops Office from launching such payloads?
tasks.notes: Asks for the control that stops Office launching payloads.

tasks.question: Excel files with macros are dropping executables into user folders and running them. How do we stop Excel itself from starting other programs?
tasks.notes: Office spawning processes is what the rule blocks.

tasks.question: Employees regularly click links in emails that impersonate our CEO. What should we invest in so staff recognise and report these messages?
tasks.notes: Explicitly about staff recognising and reporting.

tasks.question: A red-team exercise showed that 30% of staff entered credentials on a fake invoice portal sent by email. Which action targets that behaviour?
tasks.notes: Human behaviour, not a technical control.

tasks.question: How should we respond to CVE-2024-3400 on the Palo Alto firewall that terminates our remote-access VPN?
tasks.notes: Internet-facing appliance with unauthenticated RCE.
